      - no well on the plate holds this
  nowhere (standards): expected 0.39 ul bsa, 49.61 ul water; found nothing
      - no well on the plate holds this
  well A7: expected nothing; found nothing
      - the plate map says nothing about this well, but it holds liquid
  well A8: expected nothing; found nothing
      - the plate map says nothing about this well, but it holds liquid

Labware for the technique (Serial dilution): nothing to flag.

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  bsa                                   100.0      98.4       0.0       0.0     1.6
  water                                 400.0     201.6     150.0       0.0    48.4
  Note: 1.6 ul of bsa is lost: it left the deck inside a tip that was thrown away.
  Note: 48.4 ul of water is lost: it left the deck inside a tip that was thrown away.

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  1    NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL          A1    water                                350.0     400.0
  2    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A1    bsa                                  100.0     100.0  <-- NO MARGIN
  FLAG: bsa in A1, slot 2 has no margin: the robot draws 100 ul of the 100 ul declared, and
    a pipette cannot empty a tube to the last drop. Fix: in load_liquid for this well,

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 2 warnings, 1 note).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 1: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 38:  p300.aspirate(diluent_vol, water_reservoir)
   At line 38 the p300_single_gen2 draws 50 ul from water (well A1 in slot 1) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 150 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.75 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it twice, after 5 times in the liquid; 100 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 2 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 1.
   Also reached 2 other wells: wells A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [9bd1603db091]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: well A7 in slot 3
   line 42:  p300.aspirate(transfer_vol, source)
   At line 42 the tip went into well A7 in slot 3 while it still carried the liquid from
   well A8 in slot 3 from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little
   of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not
   belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but
   what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A7 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 42 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [a6713f94a36c]

3. WARNING CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried water (well A1 in slot 1) and the liquid from
well A7 in slot 3 into 2 wells it was never meant for
   line 42:  p300.aspirate(transfer_vol, source)
   At line 42 the tip touched the liquid in wells A1 and A6 in slot 3 while it still carried
   water (well A1 in slot 1) and the liquid from well A7 in slot 3 from an earlier step
   (this line did it twice). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the
   next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on
   purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now
   holds a little of another.
   Affected: wells A1 and A6 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 42. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [c0859c636fbe]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 6 wells of bsa
   line 43:  p300.dispense(transfer_vol, well)
   At line 43 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR
   Full Skirt (slot 3): 6 wells at 6 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than
   the one before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank:
   the curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic
   cannot be told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 3.
   Fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [a8b85aaee37e]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
